214                       // Change scan-cell SE only while the raw scan clock is low. The parser leaves
215                       // SCAN_DFT_SHIFT on the final rising edge; a combinational state decode would

177                       // HOST_CYCLE_END from the FPGA scheduler is the sole boundary trigger.
178                       // DRAIN waits for all internal work, WRITEBACK flushes dirty combinational
179                       // words, INVALIDATE clears cache valids, SEND_DONE emits DUT_DONE, and
180                       // WAIT_ACK prevents the next epoch from starting too early.

                   ==>  MISSING_ELSE

380                       end
381                     
382                       // A non-joined write miss issues the same four-byte backing read as a read
383                       // MSHR. Its stored mask/data are applied only when that response returns.
384                       always_comb begin
385        1/1              wm_issue_found = 1'b0;
386        1/1              wm_issue_slot = wm_issue_rr_r;
387        1/1              for (int unsigned offset = 0; offset < WRITE_MISS_ENTRIES; offset++) begin
388        1/1                if (!wm_issue_found &&
389                               wm_state_r[(wm_issue_rr_r + offset) % WRITE_MISS_ENTRIES] == WM_REQUESTING) begin
390        0/1     ==>          wm_issue_found = 1'b1;
391        0/1     ==>          wm_issue_slot = (wm_issue_rr_r + offset) % WRITE_MISS_ENTRIES;
392                           end
                        MISSING_ELSE
393                         end
394                       end
395                     
396                       // Replay one completed read to all clients that merged onto its word.
397                       // There is no response-ready signal in the tile protocol, so the client bit
398                       // is consumed when the one-cycle response is emitted. The arbiter is
399                       // expected to consume that response and the tile must be ready when it has
400                       // an outstanding accepted read.
401                       always_comb begin
402        1/1              replay_found = 1'b0;
403        1/1              replay_slot = '0;
404        1/1              replay_client = '0;
405        1/1              for (int unsigned slot = 0; slot < MSHRS; slot++) begin
406        1/1                for (int unsigned client = 0; client < VS_CLIENT_IDS; client++) begin
407        1/1                  if (!replay_found && mshr_state_r[slot] == MSHR_REPLAYING &&
408                                 mshr_clients_r[slot][client]) begin
409        1/1                    replay_found = 1'b1;
410        1/1                    replay_slot = slot[MSHR_W-1:0];
411        1/1                    replay_client = client[2:0];
412                             end
                        MISSING_ELSE
413                           end
414                         end
415                       end
416                     
417                       // Response context is local metadata. The FPGA only preserves ordering;
418                       // these values let us route the response to MSHR, direct-write, or WB logic.
419                       // Context values 0..MSHRS-1 identify read MSHRs. The reserved values 16 and
420                       // 17 identify the direct write and writeback paths. Values beginning at 18
421                       // identify parameterized write-miss entries.
422                       assign rsp_is_mshr = backing_if.rsp.response_context < MSHRS;
423                       assign rsp_mshr_slot = backing_if.rsp.response_context[MSHR_W-1:0];
424                       assign rsp_is_write_miss =
425                           backing_if.rsp.response_context >= RESPONSE_CONTEXT_WRITE_MISS_BASE &&
426                           backing_if.rsp.response_context < RESPONSE_CONTEXT_WRITE_MISS_BASE + WRITE_MISS_ENTRIES;
427                       assign rsp_wm_slot = backing_if.rsp.response_context - RESPONSE_CONTEXT_WRITE_MISS_BASE;
428                       assign rsp_is_direct = backing_if.rsp.response_context == RESPONSE_CONTEXT_TILE_WRITE;
429                       assign rsp_is_wb = backing_if.rsp.response_context == RESPONSE_CONTEXT_WRITEBACK;
430                     
431                       always_comb begin
432                         // A response is accepted only when its owner can commit the result. If the
433                         // cache is busy with a synchronous lookup or boundary walk, rsp_ready is
434                         // held low and the memory link keeps the response stable.
435        1/1              rsp_wm_match_found = 1'b0;
436        1/1              rsp_wm_match_slot = '0;
437        1/1              mshr_rsp_ready = 1'b0;
438        1/1              wm_rsp_ready = 1'b0;
439        1/1              if (rsp_is_mshr) begin
440        1/1                mshr_rsp_ready = mshr_state_r[rsp_mshr_slot] == MSHR_WRITE_TO_SRAM &&
441                                            !lookup_pending_r && wb_walk_state_r == WB_IDLE && cache_available;
442        1/1                for (int unsigned slot = 0; slot < WRITE_MISS_ENTRIES; slot++) begin
443        1/1                  if (!rsp_wm_match_found && wm_state_r[slot] == WM_JOINED &&
444                                 wm_word_addr_r[slot] == mshr_word_addr_r[rsp_mshr_slot]) begin
445        0/1     ==>            rsp_wm_match_found = 1'b1;
446        0/1     ==>            rsp_wm_match_slot = slot[WM_W-1:0];
447                             end
                        MISSING_ELSE
448                           end
449                         end
                        MISSING_ELSE
450        1/1              if (rsp_is_write_miss)
451        0/1     ==>        wm_rsp_ready = wm_state_r[rsp_wm_slot] == WM_WAITING &&
                        MISSING_ELSE
452                                          !lookup_pending_r && wb_walk_state_r == WB_IDLE && cache_available;
453                       end
454                     
455                       assign backing_if.rsp_ready = backing_if.rsp.valid &&
456                           (rsp_is_wb || rsp_is_direct || mshr_rsp_ready || wm_rsp_ready);
457                       assign backing_rsp_fire = backing_if.rsp_ready;
458                     
459                       // Dirty words always win the backing port. Consequently, a refill request
460                       // cannot overtake the writeback of the line it is about to replace.
461                       // The remaining priority is direct tile writes, write-miss reads, then
462                       // ordinary read-MSHR refills. All requests use the same ordered physical
463                       // memory link, so this priority also defines response context order.
464                       always_comb begin
465        1/1              backing_if.req = '0;
466        1/1              if (wb_count_r != 0 && !wb_issued_r) begin
467        1/1                backing_if.req.valid = 1'b1;
468        1/1                backing_if.req.write = 1'b1;
469        1/1                backing_if.req.key = {wb_addr_r[wb_head_r], 2'b00};
470        1/1                backing_if.req.wdata = wb_data_r[wb_head_r];
471        1/1                backing_if.req.wmask = 32'hffff_ffff;
472        1/1                backing_if.req.response_context = RESPONSE_CONTEXT_WRITEBACK;
473        1/1              end else if (direct_state_r == DIRECT_REQUEST) begin
474        1/1                backing_if.req.valid = 1'b1;
475        1/1                backing_if.req.write = 1'b1;
476        1/1                backing_if.req.key = {direct_req_r.addr, 2'b00};
477        1/1                backing_if.req.wdata = direct_req_r.wdata;
478        1/1                backing_if.req.wmask = direct_req_r.wmask;
479        1/1                backing_if.req.response_context = RESPONSE_CONTEXT_TILE_WRITE;
480        1/1              end else if (wb_count_r == 0 && !wb_issued_r && wm_issue_found) begin
481        0/1     ==>        backing_if.req.valid = 1'b1;
482        0/1     ==>        backing_if.req.key = {wm_word_addr_r[wm_issue_slot], 2'b00};
483        0/1     ==>        backing_if.req.response_context = RESPONSE_CONTEXT_WRITE_MISS_BASE + wm_issue_slot;
484        1/1              end else if (wb_count_r == 0 && !wb_issued_r && issue_found) begin
485        1/1                backing_if.req.valid = 1'b1;
486        1/1                backing_if.req.key = {mshr_word_addr_r[issue_slot], 2'b00};
487        1/1                backing_if.req.response_context =
488                               {{(RESPONSE_CONTEXT_W-MSHR_W){1'b0}}, issue_slot};
489                         end
                        MISSING_ELSE
490                       end
491                       assign backing_req_fire = backing_if.req.valid && backing_if.req_ready;
492                     
493                       // A replacement is queued only when the old set is valid and dirty. Clean
494                       // victims can simply be overwritten; dirty victims must reach the FPGA.
495                       assign enqueue_runtime = lookup_can_finish && !lookup_hit && cache_lookup_valid &&
496                                                cache_lookup_dirty;
497                       assign enqueue_walk = wb_walk_state_r == WB_CHECK && cache_lookup_valid &&
498                                             cache_lookup_dirty && wb_count_r < WRITEBACK_DEPTH;
499                       assign enqueue_wb = enqueue_runtime || enqueue_walk;
500                       assign enqueue_set = enqueue_runtime ? cache_set(lookup_req_r.addr) : wb_walk_set_r;
501                       assign enqueue_addr = cache_word_addr(cache_lookup_tag, enqueue_set);
502                       assign dequeue_wb = backing_rsp_fire && rsp_is_wb;
503                     
504                       // One synchronous cache port serves request lookups, refills, and the
505                       // boundary walker. Admission and response-ready prevent simultaneous users.
506                       // Refill writes have higher priority than new lookup requests because the
507                       // returned word must become resident before any dependent request proceeds.
508                       always_comb begin
509        1/1              cache_lookup = 1'b0;
510        1/1              cache_lookup_set = '0;
511        1/1              cache_write = 1'b0;
512        1/1              cache_write_set = '0;
513        1/1              cache_write_valid = 1'b1;
514        1/1              cache_write_dirty = 1'b0;
515        1/1              cache_write_tag = '0;
516        1/1              cache_write_data = '0;
517                     
518        1/1              if (lookup_req_r.write && lookup_can_finish && lookup_hit) begin
519        1/1                cache_write = 1'b1;
520        1/1                cache_write_set = cache_set(lookup_req_r.addr);
521        1/1                cache_write_tag = cache_tag(lookup_req_r.addr);
522        1/1                cache_write_data = lookup_write_value;
523        1/1                cache_write_dirty = 1'b1;
524        1/1              end else if (backing_rsp_fire && rsp_is_mshr &&
525                                      address_region(mshr_word_addr_r[rsp_mshr_slot]) != REGION_INFER &&
526                                      HAS_CACHE && control_if.control.cfg.cache_enable) begin
527        1/1                cache_write = 1'b1;
528        1/1                cache_write_set = cache_set(mshr_word_addr_r[rsp_mshr_slot]);
529        1/1                cache_write_tag = cache_tag(mshr_word_addr_r[rsp_mshr_slot]);
530        1/1                cache_write_data = rsp_wm_match_found ?
531                               masked_merge(backing_if.rsp.rdata, wm_data_r[rsp_wm_match_slot],
532                                            wm_mask_r[rsp_wm_match_slot]) : backing_if.rsp.rdata;
533        1/1                cache_write_dirty = rsp_wm_match_found;
534        1/1              end else if (backing_rsp_fire && rsp_is_write_miss && HAS_CACHE && control_if.control.cfg.cache_enable) begin
535        0/1     ==>        cache_write = 1'b1;
536        0/1     ==>        cache_write_set = cache_set(wm_word_addr_r[rsp_wm_slot]);
537        0/1     ==>        cache_write_tag = cache_tag(wm_word_addr_r[rsp_wm_slot]);
538        0/1     ==>        cache_write_data = masked_merge(backing_if.rsp.rdata, wm_data_r[rsp_wm_slot],
539                                                           wm_mask_r[rsp_wm_slot]);
540        0/1     ==>        cache_write_dirty = 1'b1;
541        1/1              end else if (wb_walk_state_r == WB_READ) begin
542        1/1                cache_lookup = 1'b1;
543        1/1                cache_lookup_set = wb_walk_set_r;
544        1/1              end else if (request_accept && request_lookup && !request_merge) begin
545        1/1                cache_lookup = 1'b1;
546        1/1                cache_lookup_set = cache_set(vs_if.req.addr);
547                         end
                        MISSING_ELSE
548                       end
549                     
550                       mem_io_cache #(
551                         .SETS (CACHE_SETS)
552                       ) i_vs_cache_bank (
553                         .clk_i, .rst_ni, .dft_shift_i,
554                         .invalidate_i (control_if.control.cache_invalidate),
555                         .available_o (cache_available), .invalidated_o (cache_invalidated),
556                         .lookup_i (cache_lookup), .lookup_set_i (cache_lookup_set),
557                         .lookup_valid_o (cache_lookup_valid), .lookup_dirty_o (cache_lookup_dirty),
558                         .lookup_tag_o (cache_lookup_tag), .lookup_data_o (cache_lookup_data),
559                         .dirty_any_o (cache_dirty_any), .dirty_set_o (cache_dirty_set),
560                         .clear_dirty_i (enqueue_walk), .clear_dirty_set_i (wb_walk_set_r),
561                         .write_i (cache_write), .write_set_i (cache_write_set),
562                         .write_valid_i (cache_write_valid), .write_dirty_i (cache_write_dirty),
563                         .write_tag_i (cache_write_tag), .write_data_i (cache_write_data)
564                       );
565                     
566                       // The arbiter sees a one-cycle response and forwards it to the tile indicated
567                       // by response_r.id. response_r.valid is cleared on the next clock because
568                       // the tile-facing protocol has no response-ready handshake.
569                       assign vs_if.rsp = response_r;
570                     
571                       always_comb begin
572                         logic mshr_idle;                        // Reduction result: all MSHRs are inactive.
573                         logic write_miss_idle;                  // Reduction result: no write refill remains.
574        1/1              mshr_idle = 1'b1;
575        1/1              for (int unsigned slot = 0; slot < MSHRS; slot++)
576        1/1                mshr_idle &= mshr_state_r[slot] == MSHR_INACTIVE;
577        1/1              write_miss_idle = 1'b1;
578        1/1              for (int unsigned slot = 0; slot < WRITE_MISS_ENTRIES; slot++)
579        1/1                write_miss_idle &= wm_state_r[slot] == WM_INACTIVE;
580        1/1              control_if.vs_status.idle = mshr_idle && write_miss_idle && !lookup_pending_r &&
581                                         direct_state_r == DIRECT_IDLE &&
582                                         wb_count_r == 0 && !wb_issued_r && !response_r.valid &&
583                                         wb_walk_state_r == WB_IDLE && cache_available;
584        1/1              control_if.vs_status.invalidated = !HAS_CACHE || cache_invalidated;
585        1/1              control_if.vs_status.writeback_done = !HAS_CACHE ||
586                           !control_if.control.cfg.cache_enable || wb_walk_done_r;
587                       end
588                     
589                       // All MSHR, lookup, direct-write, response, and writeback state changes are
590                       // committed on this edge. Combinational blocks above only propose actions.
591                       always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
592        1/1              if (!rst_ni) begin
593        1/1                for (int unsigned slot = 0; slot < MSHRS; slot++) begin
594        1/1                  mshr_state_r[slot] <= MSHR_INACTIVE;
595        1/1                  mshr_data_r[slot] <= '0;
596        1/1                  mshr_word_addr_r[slot] <= '0;
597        1/1                  mshr_clients_r[slot] <= '0;
598                           end
599        1/1                for (int unsigned slot = 0; slot < WRITE_MISS_ENTRIES; slot++) begin
600        1/1                  wm_state_r[slot] <= WM_INACTIVE;
601        1/1                  wm_word_addr_r[slot] <= '0;
602        1/1                  wm_data_r[slot] <= '0;
603        1/1                  wm_mask_r[slot] <= '0;
604                           end
605        1/1                lookup_pending_r <= 1'b0;
606        1/1                lookup_req_r <= '0;
607        1/1                direct_state_r <= DIRECT_IDLE;
608        1/1                direct_req_r <= '0;
609        1/1                wb_head_r <= '0;
610        1/1                wb_tail_r <= '0;
611        1/1                wb_count_r <= '0;
612        1/1                wb_issued_r <= 1'b0;
613        1/1                wb_walk_state_r <= WB_IDLE;
614        1/1                wb_walk_set_r <= '0;
615        1/1                wb_walk_done_r <= 1'b0;
616        1/1                response_r <= '0;
617        1/1                issue_rr_r <= '0;
618        1/1                wm_issue_rr_r <= '0;
619                         end else begin
620        1/1                response_r.valid <= 1'b0;
621                     
622                           // New requests merge with pending work, start one cache lookup, or enter
623                           // the narrow direct-write slot used by uncached regions.
624        1/1                if (request_accept) begin
625        1/1                  if (request_merge) begin
626        0/1     ==>            mshr_clients_r[match_slot] <= mshr_clients_r[match_slot] | vs_if.req.id;
627        1/1                  end else if (request_merge_write) begin
628        0/1     ==>            wm_data_r[wm_match_slot] <= masked_merge(wm_data_r[wm_match_slot],
629                                                                        vs_if.req.wdata,
630                                                                        vs_if.req.wmask);
631        0/1     ==>            wm_mask_r[wm_match_slot] <= wm_mask_r[wm_match_slot] | vs_if.req.wmask;
632        1/1                  end else if (request_join_read) begin
633        0/1     ==>            wm_state_r[wm_free_slot] <= WM_JOINED;
634        0/1     ==>            wm_word_addr_r[wm_free_slot] <= vs_if.req.addr;
635        0/1     ==>            wm_data_r[wm_free_slot] <= vs_if.req.wdata;
636        0/1     ==>            wm_mask_r[wm_free_slot] <= vs_if.req.wmask;
637        1/1                  end else if (request_lookup) begin
638        1/1                    lookup_pending_r <= 1'b1;
639        1/1                    lookup_req_r <= vs_if.req;
640        1/1                  end else if (request_bypass_read) begin
641        1/1                    mshr_state_r[free_slot] <= MSHR_REQUESTING;
642        1/1                    mshr_word_addr_r[free_slot] <= vs_if.req.addr;
643        1/1                    mshr_clients_r[free_slot] <= vs_if.req.id;
644                             end else begin
645        1/1                    direct_state_r <= DIRECT_REQUEST;
646        1/1                    direct_req_r <= vs_if.req;
647                             end
648                           end
                        MISSING_ELSE
649                     
650                           // Complete the one-cycle synchronous cache lookup. A write hit is written
651                           // immediately. A write miss creates a write-miss entry and waits for the
652                           // FPGA's current word. A read miss creates an MSHR and waits for refill.
653        1/1                if (lookup_can_finish) begin
654        1/1                  lookup_pending_r <= 1'b0;
655        1/1                  if (lookup_req_r.write) begin
656                               // Hits merge immediately. Misses retain data and mask until a
657                               // backing read supplies authoritative masked-off bits.
658        1/1                    if (!lookup_hit) begin
659        0/1     ==>              wm_state_r[wm_free_slot] <= WM_REQUESTING;
660        0/1     ==>              wm_word_addr_r[wm_free_slot] <= lookup_req_r.addr;
661        0/1     ==>              wm_data_r[wm_free_slot] <= lookup_req_r.wdata;
662        0/1     ==>              wm_mask_r[wm_free_slot] <= lookup_req_r.wmask;
663                               end
                        MISSING_ELSE
664        1/1                  end else if (lookup_hit) begin
665        1/1                    response_r.valid <= 1'b1;
666        1/1                    response_r.id <= lookup_req_r.id;
667        1/1                    response_r.rdata <= cache_lookup_data;
668                             end else begin
669        1/1                    mshr_state_r[free_slot] <= MSHR_REQUESTING;
670        1/1                    mshr_word_addr_r[free_slot] <= lookup_req_r.addr;
671        1/1                    mshr_clients_r[free_slot] <= lookup_req_r.id;
672                             end
673                           end
                        MISSING_ELSE
674                     
675                           // Once a request leaves for the FPGA, mark its context outstanding.
676                           // This prevents a second issue from reusing the same MSHR prematurely.
677        1/1                if (backing_req_fire) begin
678        1/1                  if (backing_if.req.response_context == RESPONSE_CONTEXT_WRITEBACK)
679        1/1                    wb_issued_r <= 1'b1;
680        1/1                  else if (backing_if.req.response_context == RESPONSE_CONTEXT_TILE_WRITE)
681        1/1                    direct_state_r <= DIRECT_WAIT;
682        1/1                  else if (backing_if.req.response_context >= RESPONSE_CONTEXT_WRITE_MISS_BASE) begin
683        0/1     ==>            wm_state_r[wm_issue_slot] <= WM_WAITING;
684        0/1     ==>            wm_issue_rr_r <= wm_issue_slot + 1'b1;
685                             end
686                             else begin
687        1/1                    mshr_state_r[issue_slot] <= MSHR_WRITE_TO_SRAM;
688        1/1                    issue_rr_r <= issue_slot + 1'b1;
689                             end
690                           end
                        MISSING_ELSE
691                     
692                           // Ordered FPGA responses complete the context that occupied the head of
693                           // the link's metadata FIFO. A refill enters replay; writes return idle.
694                           // A write-miss response is never installed as the raw FPGA word. It is
695                           // always merged with the saved wmask so masked-off bits come from the
696                           // authoritative backing value and cannot be overwritten by stale CMTE
697                           // snapshot bits.
698        1/1                if (backing_rsp_fire) begin
699        1/1                  if (rsp_is_wb) begin
700        1/1                    wb_issued_r <= 1'b0;
701        1/1                  end else if (rsp_is_direct) begin
702        1/1                    direct_state_r <= DIRECT_IDLE;
703        1/1                  end else if (rsp_is_write_miss) begin
704        0/1     ==>            wm_state_r[rsp_wm_slot] <= WM_INACTIVE;
705        0/1     ==>            wm_mask_r[rsp_wm_slot] <= '0;
706        1/1                  end else if (rsp_is_mshr) begin
707        1/1                    if (rsp_wm_match_found) begin
708        0/1     ==>              mshr_data_r[rsp_mshr_slot] <=
709                                     masked_merge(backing_if.rsp.rdata, wm_data_r[rsp_wm_match_slot],
710                                                  wm_mask_r[rsp_wm_match_slot]);
711        0/1     ==>              wm_state_r[rsp_wm_match_slot] <= WM_INACTIVE;
712        0/1     ==>              wm_mask_r[rsp_wm_match_slot] <= '0;
713                               end else begin
714        1/1                      mshr_data_r[rsp_mshr_slot] <= backing_if.rsp.rdata;
715                               end
716        1/1                    mshr_state_r[rsp_mshr_slot] <= MSHR_REPLAYING;
717                             end
                   ==>  MISSING_ELSE
718                           end
                        MISSING_ELSE
719                     
720                           // Replays are one-hot because the tile-facing response carries one
721                           // engine destination per cycle. Data remains frozen for the full replay.
722        1/1                if (!response_r.valid && !lookup_can_finish &&
723                               replay_found) begin
724        1/1                  response_r.valid <= 1'b1;
725        1/1                  response_r.id <= 8'b1 << replay_client;
726        1/1                  response_r.rdata <= mshr_data_r[replay_slot];
727        1/1                  mshr_clients_r[replay_slot][replay_client] <= 1'b0;
728        1/1                  if ((mshr_clients_r[replay_slot] & ~(8'b1 << replay_client)) == 0)
729        1/1                    mshr_state_r[replay_slot] <= MSHR_INACTIVE;
                   ==>  MISSING_ELSE
730                           end
                        MISSING_ELSE
731                     
732                           // Ring-buffer pointer updates support enqueue and dequeue in one cycle.
733                           // enqueue_wb is generated for dirty runtime victims and for dirty lines
734                           // found by the boundary walker. The queue stores complete words, so the
735                           // backing writeback always uses an all-one mask.
736        1/1                if (enqueue_wb) begin
737        1/1                  wb_addr_r[wb_tail_r] <= enqueue_addr;
738        1/1                  wb_data_r[wb_tail_r] <= cache_lookup_data;
739        1/1                  wb_tail_r <= wb_tail_r == WRITEBACK_DEPTH-1 ? '0 : wb_tail_r + 1'b1;
740                           end
                        MISSING_ELSE
741        1/1                if (dequeue_wb)
742        1/1                  wb_head_r <= wb_head_r == WRITEBACK_DEPTH-1 ? '0 : wb_head_r + 1'b1;
                        MISSING_ELSE
743        1/1                unique case ({enqueue_wb, dequeue_wb})
744        1/1                  2'b10: wb_count_r <= wb_count_r + 1'b1;
745        1/1                  2'b01: wb_count_r <= wb_count_r - 1'b1;
746                             default: begin end
747                           endcase
748                     
749                           // Boundary writeback priority-selects only valid dirty sets. WB_READ
750                           // fetches the selected SRAM word, WB_CHECK copies it into the writeback
751                           // FIFO and clears its dirty bit, and WB_DRAIN waits for all FPGA writes.
752                           // Clean entries are never read. Invalidation later clears all metadata
753                           // together, preserving dirty COMB state without a 128-set linear walk.
754        1/1                if (!control_if.control.vs_writeback) begin
755        1/1                  wb_walk_state_r <= WB_IDLE;
756        1/1                  wb_walk_done_r <= 1'b0;
757                           end else begin
758        1/1                  unique case (wb_walk_state_r)
759                               WB_IDLE: begin
760        1/1                      if (!wb_walk_done_r) begin

                   -17-  
700                  wb_issued_r <= 1'b0;
                     ==>
701                end else if (rsp_is_direct) begin
                            -18-  
702                  direct_state_r <= DIRECT_IDLE;
                     ==>
703                end else if (rsp_is_write_miss) begin
                            -19-  
704                  wm_state_r[rsp_wm_slot] <= WM_INACTIVE;
                     ==>
705                  wm_mask_r[rsp_wm_slot] <= '0;
706                end else if (rsp_is_mshr) begin
                            -20-  
707                  if (rsp_wm_match_found) begin
                     -21-  
708                    mshr_data_r[rsp_mshr_slot] <=
                       ==>
709                        masked_merge(backing_if.rsp.rdata, wm_data_r[rsp_wm_match_slot],
710                                     wm_mask_r[rsp_wm_match_slot]);
711                    wm_state_r[rsp_wm_match_slot] <= WM_INACTIVE;
712                    wm_mask_r[rsp_wm_match_slot] <= '0;
713                  end else begin
714                    mshr_data_r[rsp_mshr_slot] <= backing_if.rsp.rdata;
                       ==>
715                  end
716                  mshr_state_r[rsp_mshr_slot] <= MSHR_REPLAYING;
717                end
                   MISSING_ELSE
                   ==>
718              end
                 MISSING_ELSE
                 ==>
719        
720              // Replays are one-hot because the tile-facing response carries one
721              // engine destination per cycle. Data remains frozen for the full replay.
722              if (!response_r.valid && !lookup_can_finish &&
                 -22-  
723                  replay_found) begin
724                response_r.valid <= 1'b1;
725                response_r.id <= 8'b1 << replay_client;
726                response_r.rdata <= mshr_data_r[replay_slot];
727                mshr_clients_r[replay_slot][replay_client] <= 1'b0;
728                if ((mshr_clients_r[replay_slot] & ~(8'b1 << replay_client)) == 0)
                   -23-  
729                  mshr_state_r[replay_slot] <= MSHR_INACTIVE;
                     ==>
                     MISSING_ELSE
                     ==>
730              end
                 MISSING_ELSE
                 ==>
731        
732              // Ring-buffer pointer updates support enqueue and dequeue in one cycle.
733              // enqueue_wb is generated for dirty runtime victims and for dirty lines
734              // found by the boundary walker. The queue stores complete words, so the
735              // backing writeback always uses an all-one mask.
736              if (enqueue_wb) begin
                 -24-  
737                wb_addr_r[wb_tail_r] <= enqueue_addr;
738                wb_data_r[wb_tail_r] <= cache_lookup_data;
739                wb_tail_r <= wb_tail_r == WRITEBACK_DEPTH-1 ? '0 : wb_tail_r + 1'b1;
                                                               -25-  
                                                               ==>  
                                                               ==>  
740              end
                 MISSING_ELSE
                 ==>
741              if (dequeue_wb)
                 -26-  
742                wb_head_r <= wb_head_r == WRITEBACK_DEPTH-1 ? '0 : wb_head_r + 1'b1;
                                                               -27-  
                                                               ==>  
                                                               ==>  
                   MISSING_ELSE
                   ==>
743              unique case ({enqueue_wb, dequeue_wb})
                        -28-  
744                2'b10: wb_count_r <= wb_count_r + 1'b1;
                   ==>
745                2'b01: wb_count_r <= wb_count_r - 1'b1;
                   ==>
746                default: begin end
                   ==>
747              endcase
748        
749              // Boundary writeback priority-selects only valid dirty sets. WB_READ
750              // fetches the selected SRAM word, WB_CHECK copies it into the writeback
751              // FIFO and clears its dirty bit, and WB_DRAIN waits for all FPGA writes.
752              // Clean entries are never read. Invalidation later clears all metadata
753              // together, preserving dirty COMB state without a 128-set linear walk.
754              if (!control_if.control.vs_writeback) begin
                 -29-             
755                wb_walk_state_r <= WB_IDLE;
                   ==>
756                wb_walk_done_r <= 1'b0;
757              end else begin
758                unique case (wb_walk_state_r)
                          -30-  
759                  WB_IDLE: begin
760                    if (!wb_walk_done_r) begin
                       -31-  
761                      if (cache_dirty_any) begin
                         -32-  
762                        wb_walk_set_r <= cache_dirty_set;
                           ==>
763                        wb_walk_state_r <= WB_READ;
764                      end else begin
765                        wb_walk_state_r <= WB_DRAIN;
                           ==>
766                      end
767                    end
                       MISSING_ELSE
                       ==>
768                  end
769                  WB_READ: wb_walk_state_r <= WB_CHECK;
                     ==>
770                  WB_CHECK: begin
771                    if (!cache_lookup_valid || !cache_lookup_dirty ||
                       -33-  
772                        wb_count_r < WRITEBACK_DEPTH) begin
773                      wb_walk_state_r <= WB_IDLE;
                         ==>
774                    end
                       MISSING_ELSE
                       ==>
775                  end
776                  WB_DRAIN: begin
777                    if (wb_count_r == 0 && !wb_issued_r) begin
                       -34-  
778                      wb_walk_done_r <= 1'b1;
                         ==>
779                      wb_walk_state_r <= WB_IDLE;
780                    end
                       MISSING_ELSE
                       ==>

104                       // or ENDC behind back_reg), back_reg's word is still waiting for its
105                       // datapath handoff, and no handoff is being presented. A sequential
106                       // producer cannot reach that word's LD b=1 past the stalled command, so
107                       // the engine is stuck for good: the program broke the one-word-pending
108                       // rule (INSTRUCTION_REFERENCE LD) or dropped an LD b=1. The window only
109                       // absorbs producer pipeline latency between executing an LD and raising
110                       // dp_valid_i; a legal program never holds this signature at all.

154                       // INDEX publishes its assembled response. IDXPUSH supplies a base address;
155                       // fused capture supplies the already-resolved LOADB effective address.
156                       assign index_op_valid_o = !initialize &&
157                         (state == PUBLISH_INDEX || (state == COMMAND && command_count != 0 && needs_index_op));
158                       assign index_op_o = state == PUBLISH_INDEX ? IDX_SET : is_push ? IDX_PUSH : IDX_CAPTURE;
159                       assign index_data_o = state == PUBLISH_INDEX ? index_assembly :
160                         is_push ? head_cmd.address : effective_address;
161                     
162                       // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
163                       // Generate an aligned value-store memory request
164                       // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
165                     
166                       assign request_valid_o = !reset_i && state == WAIT_ACK;
167                       // Dropping two address bits converts bytes into aligned words.
168                       assign request_address_o = byte_address[ADDR_SPACE_WIDTH-1:TILE_WORD_BYTE_IDX];
169                     
170                       // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
171                       // Accept and format a returned memory word
172                       // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
173                     
174                       // Also handle a response arriving alongside its ACK.
175                       assign response_accept = !reset_i && response_valid_i && (state == WAIT_RESPONSE ||
176                         (state == WAIT_ACK && request_ack_i));
177                       // Compact selected source bits into consecutive low positions.
178                       function automatic logic [TILE_BYTE_WIDTH-1:0] gather_byte(
179                         input logic [TILE_BYTE_WIDTH-1:0] source_byte, gather_mask
180                       );
181                         logic [TILE_BYTE_WIDTH-1:0] packed_bits;
182                         int position;
183        0/1     ==>      position = 0;
184        0/1     ==>      packed_bits = 0;
185        0/1     ==>      for (int bit_index = 0; bit_index < TILE_BYTE_WIDTH; bit_index++) begin
186        0/1     ==>        if (gather_mask[bit_index]) begin
187        0/1     ==>          packed_bits[position] = source_byte[bit_index];
188        0/1     ==>          position++;
189                           end
                   ==>  MISSING_ELSE
190                         end
191        0/1     ==>      return packed_bits;
192                       endfunction
193                     
194                       // Number of useful bytes in this aligned-word response.
195                       assign word_bytes_left = CHUNK_BYTES_W'(TILE_WORD_BYTES) -
196                         CHUNK_BYTES_W'(byte_address[TILE_WORD_BYTE_IDX-1:0]);
197                       assign chunk_bytes = bytes_remaining < TILE_LOADB_BYTE_COUNT_WIDTH'(word_bytes_left)
198                         ? CHUNK_BYTES_W'(bytes_remaining) : word_bytes_left;
199                       // Move the first requested byte into the low byte.
200                       assign shifted = response_data_i >> {byte_address[TILE_WORD_BYTE_IDX-1:0], TILE_BYTE_IDX'(0)};
201                       always_comb begin
202        1/1              if (active_cmd.gather) begin
203        0/1     ==>        chunk_bits = WORD_BIT_COUNT_WIDTH'($countones(active_cmd.gather_mask));
204        0/1     ==>        chunk_data = WORD_WIDTH'(gather_byte(shifted[TILE_BYTE_WIDTH-1:0],active_cmd.gather_mask));
205                         end else begin
206                           // A final RF DATA byte may be partial; INDEX responses use complete bytes.
207        1/1                chunk_bits = !active_cmd.index_value &&
208                             bytes_remaining == TILE_LOADB_BYTE_COUNT_WIDTH'(chunk_bytes)
209                             ? (((WORD_BIT_COUNT_WIDTH'(chunk_bytes) - 1'b1) << TILE_BYTE_IDX) + active_last_bits)
210                             : WORD_BIT_COUNT_WIDTH'(chunk_bytes) << TILE_BYTE_IDX;
211        1/1                chunk_data = shifted & low_mask(chunk_bits);
212                         end
213                       end
214                       assign index_response = response_accept && active_cmd.index_value;
215                       assign final_response = response_accept && bytes_remaining == TILE_LOADB_BYTE_COUNT_WIDTH'(chunk_bytes);
216                     
217                       // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
218                       // Pack formatted responses into complete back-register-file writes
219                       // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
220                     
221                       // INDEX responses bypass the RF packer.
222                       assign fragment_push = response_accept && !active_cmd.index_value;
223                     
224                       rf_packer packer (
225                         .clk_i, .reset_i, .clear_i(endl_valid_o && endl_ready_i),
226                         .push_i(fragment_push), .push_data_i(chunk_data), .push_bits_i(chunk_bits),
227                         .push_cursor_i(destination_cursor), .space_o(fragment_space),
228                         .drain_i(state == DRAIN_ENDL), .empty_o(packer_empty),
229                         .rf_write_o, .rf_address_o, .rf_data_o
230                       );
231                     
232                       // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
233                       // Control FSM
234                       // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
235                     
236                       // State transitions have explicit, mutually exclusive priorities.
237                       always_comb begin
238        1/1              case (state)
239                           COMMAND:
240        1/1                  next_state = command_pop && is_endl ? DRAIN_ENDL :
241                               start_load ? RESERVE_RESPONSE : COMMAND;
242                           // No response backpressure: reserve capacity before asserting valid.
243                           RESERVE_RESPONSE:
244        1/1                  next_state = fragment_space ? WAIT_ACK : RESERVE_RESPONSE;
245                           // Wait for this response before issuing another read.
246                           WAIT_ACK, WAIT_RESPONSE:
247        1/1                  if (final_response)
248        1/1                    next_state = index_response ? PUBLISH_INDEX : COMMAND;
249        2/2                  else if (response_accept) next_state = RESERVE_RESPONSE;
250        2/2                  else if (request_ack_i && state == WAIT_ACK) next_state = WAIT_RESPONSE;
251        1/1                  else next_state = state;
252                           PUBLISH_INDEX:
253        0/1     ==>          next_state = index_op_ready_i ? COMMAND : PUBLISH_INDEX;
254                           // Earlier requests finished; drain fragments and flush the final RF word.
255                           DRAIN_ENDL:
256        1/1                  next_state = endl_valid_o && endl_ready_i ? COMMAND : DRAIN_ENDL;
257        1/1                default: next_state = COMMAND;
258                         endcase
259                       end
260                     
261                       always_ff @(posedge clk_i) begin
262                         // Controller and lifecycle state.
263        1/1              state <= (initialize ? COMMAND : next_state);
264        2/2              if (initialize || command_push) busy_o <= !initialize;
                        MISSING_ELSE
265                         // Enqueued ENDL closes ingress immediately, before it retires.
266        1/1              if (initialize || (command_push && cmd_i.kind == LOAD_END))
267        1/1                endl_accepted <= !initialize;
                        MISSING_ELSE
268                         // Command FIFO storage and pointers.
269                         // Simultaneous enqueue and dequeue leave occupancy unchanged.
270        1/1              command_count <= initialize ? '0 :
271                           command_count + COUNT_W'(command_push) - COUNT_W'(command_pop);
272        1/1              if (initialize || command_push)
273        1/1                command_write_ptr <= initialize ? '0 : next_ptr(command_write_ptr);
                        MISSING_ELSE
274        1/1              if (initialize || command_pop)
275        1/1                command_read_ptr <= initialize ? '0 : next_ptr(command_read_ptr);
                        MISSING_ELSE
276        2/2              if (command_push) command_fifo[command_write_ptr] <= cmd_i;
                        MISSING_ELSE
277                     
278                         // Reserve the entire destination before any response arrives.
279        1/1              if (initialize || (start_load && !index_form))
280        1/1                allocation_cursor <= initialize ? '0 : aligned_cursor + instruction_bits;
                        MISSING_ELSE
281                     
282                         // Address/request tracking.
283                         // Full-address loads establish the base for subsequent near loads.
284        1/1              if (initialize || (start_load && !near_form)) begin
285        1/1                load_base <= initialize ? '0 : effective_address;
286                         end
                        MISSING_ELSE
287                         // Retain operands while the FIFO advances to later commands.
288        2/2              if (start_load) active_cmd <= '{index_value:index_form, gather:bits_form,
                        MISSING_ELSE
289                           gather_mask:head_cmd.gather_mask, last_bits_m1:head_cmd.last_bits_m1};
290        1/1              if (start_load || (response_accept && !final_response)) begin
291        1/1                byte_address <= start_load ? effective_address : byte_address + ADDR_SPACE_WIDTH'(chunk_bytes);
292        1/1                bytes_remaining <= start_load ? head_cmd.byte_count :
293                             bytes_remaining - TILE_LOADB_BYTE_COUNT_WIDTH'(chunk_bytes);
294                         end
                        MISSING_ELSE
295        1/1              if (initialize || start_load || response_accept)
296        1/1                destination_cursor <= initialize ? '0 : start_load ? aligned_cursor : destination_cursor + RF_BIT_CURSOR_WIDTH'(chunk_bits);
                        MISSING_ELSE
297                     
298                         // INDEX response assembly.
299                         // Assemble little-endian index bytes, including across word boundaries.
300        1/1              if (initialize || start_index || index_response)
301        1/1                index_assembly <= initialize || start_index ? '0 :
                        MISSING_ELSE
302                             index_assembly | (chunk_data[ADDR_SPACE_WIDTH-1:0] << index_shift);
303        1/1              if (initialize || start_index || index_response)
304        1/1                index_shift <= initialize || start_index ? '0 : index_shift + (INDEX_SHIFT_W'(chunk_bytes) << TILE_BYTE_IDX);

314                       // holds nothing (e.g. the tile's first dispatch after reset). Only the
315                       // rising edge is checked -- clear itself resets the state that proves it.
316                       // tile_cmte checks the front end's half.
317                       clear_needs_quiescent_be: assert property (@(posedge clk_i) disable iff (reset_i)
318                         $rose(clear_i) |-> (program_done_o ||
319                                             ((endc_state_r == ENDC_IDLE) && be_drained && !back_reg_valid_r)))
320                         else $error("back_end: clear_i while the back end still holds work");
321                     
322                       // consume requires wr_valid_r, ship_u2d requires wr_free -- they can
323                       // never coincide, so delta_acc_r never changes out from under the
324                       // snapshot delta takes of it.
325                       commit_ship_mutex: assert property (@(posedge clk_i) disable iff (reset_i)
326                         !(consume && ship_u2d))
327                         else $error("back_end: commit landed the same cycle ship_u2d fired");
328                     
329                       // ---- Front-end sequencing the back end relies on ----
330                       be_push_into_free_back_reg: assert property (@(posedge clk_i) disable iff (reset_i || clear_i)
331                         back_reg_push_i |-> back_reg_free_o)
332                         else $error("back_end: back_reg push while back_reg still holds a word");
333                     
334                       // RB + skid are only safe because the front end never forwards more than
335                       // one word ahead of the seam. A forward that isn't taken is lost; one that
336                       // lands in RB past a waiting skid entry reorders words.
337                       be_fwd_never_dropped: assert property (@(posedge clk_i) disable iff (reset_i || clear_i)
338                         read_fwd_valid_i |-> read_fwd_ready_o)
339                         else $error("back_end: read forward dropped (RB and skid both full)");
340                     
341                       be_fwd_keeps_order: assert property (@(posedge clk_i) disable iff (reset_i || clear_i)
342                         !(read_fwd_valid_i && rb_empty && skid_valid_r))
343                         else $error("back_end: read forward overtook the skid entry (word order lost)");
344                     
345                       be_endc_after_seam_drained: assert property (@(posedge clk_i) disable iff (reset_i || clear_i)
346                         endc_i |-> !back_reg_valid_r)
347                         else $error("back_end: ENDC while back_reg still holds a word");
348                     
349                       // ---- Datapath handoff (F9): the producer holds A/R31 until dp_ack_o ----
350                       be_dp_holds_until_ack: assert property (@(posedge clk_i) disable iff (reset_i || clear_i)
351                         (dp_valid_i && !dp_ack_o) |=> (dp_valid_i && $stable(accumulator_i) && $stable(guards_i)))
352                         else $error("back_end: dp_valid_i/accumulator_i/guards_i changed before dp_ack_o");
353                     
354                       // ---- VS response contract: a read's rsp arrives >= 1 cycle after its ack ----
355                       be_rsp_only_when_waiting: assert property (@(posedge clk_i) disable iff (reset_i || clear_i)
356                         vs_bus.rsp_valid |-> (rb_state_r == RB_WAIT_RESP))
357                         else $error("back_end: VS rsp_valid while RB is not waiting for one (response lost)");
358                     
359                       be_done_sticky: assert property (@(posedge clk_i) disable iff (reset_i)
360                         (program_done_o && !clear_i) |=> program_done_o)
361                         else $error("back_end: program_done_o dropped before clear_i");
362                     
363                       // ---- Each value-store bit is committed at most once per image ----
364                       // A second commit of a bit can take its old value from a read issued
365                       // before the first commit's write lands, so it compares against stale data
366                       // and silently drops its own update. The ISA makes that program malformed;
367                       // this shadow of every bit committed since reset/clear catches it.
368                       logic [WORD_WIDTH-1:0] committed_bits [logic [WIDX-1:0]];
369                       always @(posedge clk_i) begin
370        1/1              if (reset_i || clear_i) begin
371        1/1                committed_bits.delete();
372        1/1              end else if (consume) begin
373        1/1                if (committed_bits.exists(wr_addr_r)) begin
374                             be_bit_committed_once: assert ((committed_bits[wr_addr_r] & back_reg_r.field) == '0)
375                               else $error("back_end: word %h commits bits %h a second time this image (malformed)",
376                                           {wr_addr_r, 2'b00}, committed_bits[wr_addr_r] & back_reg_r.field);
377        0/1     ==>          committed_bits[wr_addr_r] = committed_bits[wr_addr_r] | back_reg_r.field;
378                           end else begin
379        1/1                  committed_bits[wr_addr_r] = back_reg_r.field;
380                           end
381                         end
                        MISSING_ELSE

200                       // (back_end.md#state-ownership, #rb-and-address-skid)
201                       always_ff @(posedge clk_i) begin
202        1/1              if (reset_i || clear_i) begin
203        1/1                rb_state_r <= RB_EMPTY;
204                         end else begin
205        1/1                unique case (rb_state_r)
206                             RB_EMPTY: begin
207        1/1                    if (rb_admit_direct) begin
208        1/1                      rb_addr_r    <= read_fwd_i.addr;
209        1/1                      rb_state_r   <= read_fwd_i.no_read ? RB_RESOLVED : RB_WAIT_ACK;
210        1/1                    end else if (rb_admit_from_skid) begin
211        0/1     ==>              rb_addr_r    <= skid_addr_r;
212        0/1     ==>              rb_state_r   <= skid_no_read_r ? RB_RESOLVED : RB_WAIT_ACK;
213                               end
                        MISSING_ELSE
214                             end
215                             // stays WAIT_ACK (re-asserting vs_want_read every cycle) until VSP
216                             // reports its req acked -- ack = received, not resolved, so a READ
217                             // moves on to WAIT_RESP rather than RESOLVED
218        2/2                  RB_WAIT_ACK:  if (vsp_read_ack)      rb_state_r <= RB_WAIT_RESP;
                        MISSING_ELSE
219        2/2                  RB_WAIT_RESP: if (vs_bus.rsp_valid)  rb_state_r <= RB_RESOLVED;
                        MISSING_ELSE
220        2/2                  RB_RESOLVED:  if (rb_pop)            rb_state_r <= RB_EMPTY;
                   ==>  MISSING_ELSE
221                           endcase
222                     
223        2/2                if ((rb_state_r == RB_WAIT_RESP) && vs_bus.rsp_valid) rb_data_r <= vs_bus.rsp_rdata;
                        MISSING_ELSE
224                         end
225                       end
226                     
227                       // -- WB --
228                       always_ff @(posedge clk_i) begin
229        1/1              if (reset_i || clear_i) begin
230        1/1                wb_valid_r <= 1'b0;
231        1/1              end else if (wr_to_wb_pop) begin
232        1/1                wb_addr_r  <= wr_addr_r;
233        1/1                wb_data_r  <= wr_data_r;
234        1/1                wb_wmask_r <= wr_wmask_r;
235        1/1                wb_valid_r <= 1'b1;
236        1/1              end else if (vsp_write_ack) begin
237        1/1                wb_valid_r <= 1'b0;
238                         end
                        MISSING_ELSE
239                       end
240                     
241                       // ================= VSP =================
242                     
243                       // RB wants the port for as long as it's WAIT_ACK -- ack alone doesn't
244                       // resolve a read, so state moves to RB_WAIT_RESP
245                       logic  vs_want_read, vs_want_write;
246                       assign vs_want_read = (rb_state_r == RB_WAIT_ACK);
247                       assign vs_want_write = wb_valid_r; // WB wants port when it holds a write
248                     
249                       vsp vsp_u (
250                         .clk_i(clk_i), .reset_i(reset_i), .clear_i(clear_i),
251                     
252                         .vs_want_read_i(vs_want_read), .vs_want_write_i(vs_want_write),
253                     
254                         .rb_addr_i(rb_addr_r), .wb_addr_i(wb_addr_r),
255                         .wb_data_i(wb_data_r), .wb_wmask_i(wb_wmask_r),
256                     
257                         .read_ack_o(vsp_read_ack), .write_ack_o(vsp_write_ack),
258                     
259                         .vs_bus(vs_bus)
260                       );
261                     
262                       // ================= Delta =================
263                       // ----------------- ENDC / quiescence -----------------
264                       // be_drained: RB/WR/WB/skid all empty -- purely structural, the point
265                       // past which no further commit_valid_i can land (wr_free here is
266                       // mutually exclusive with consume's wr_valid_r). Only meaningful as the
267                       // ENDC_PENDING -> ENDC_SENT transition condition below.
268                       logic be_drained;
269                       assign be_drained = rb_empty && skid_free && wr_free && wb_free;
270                     
271                       // ship_u2d: one-shot pulse to delta, firing exactly once on the
272                       // ENDC_PENDING -> ENDC_SENT edge, telling it the accumulator is final
273                       // and safe to snapshot. delta owns the rest of the handoff itself:
274                       // delta_valid_o holds from the ship until delta_ready_i takes it, and
275                       // delta_fire is that transfer, which is what ENDC_SENT waits for.
276                       logic ship_u2d, delta_fire;
277                       assign ship_u2d   = (endc_state_r == ENDC_PENDING) && be_drained;
278                       assign delta_fire = delta_valid_o && delta_ready_i;
279                     
280                       delta delta_u (
281                         .clk_i(clk_i), .reset_i(reset_i), .clear_i(clear_i),
282                     
283                         .commit_valid_i(consume), .dirty_i(dirty),
284                         .cell_bounds_i(back_reg_r.cell_bounds), .base_class_i(back_reg_r.base_class),
285                     
286                         .ship_i(ship_u2d), .delta_ready_i(delta_ready_i),
287                     
288                         .delta_o(delta_o), .delta_valid_o(delta_valid_o)
289                       );
290                     
291                       always_ff @(posedge clk_i) begin
292        1/1              if (reset_i || clear_i) begin
293        1/1                endc_state_r <= ENDC_IDLE;
294                         end else begin
295        1/1                unique case (endc_state_r)
296        2/2                  ENDC_IDLE:     if (endc_i)         endc_state_r <= ENDC_PENDING;
                        MISSING_ELSE
297        2/2                  ENDC_PENDING:  if (be_drained)     endc_state_r <= ENDC_SENT;
                        MISSING_ELSE
298        2/2                  ENDC_SENT:     if (delta_fire)     endc_state_r <= PROG_COMPLETE;
                   ==>  MISSING_ELSE
299        1/1                  PROG_COMPLETE: ; // holds until clear_i
300                           endcase
301                         end
302                       end
303                     
304                       // program_done_o is purely registered: it rises the cycle after the Delta
305                       // transfer (by then the consumer has already taken delta_o) and holds,
306                       // sticky, until clear_i. Nothing here depends combinationally on
307                       // delta_ready_i.
308                       assign program_done_o = (endc_state_r == PROG_COMPLETE);
309                     
310                     `ifndef SYNTHESIS
311                       // Simulation-only checks are excluded by the SYNTHESIS define.
312                     
313                       // clear_i may start once the image has completed, or while the back end
314                       // holds nothing (e.g. the tile's first dispatch after reset). Only the
315                       // rising edge is checked -- clear itself resets the state that proves it.
316                       // tile_cmte checks the front end's half.
317                       clear_needs_quiescent_be: assert property (@(posedge clk_i) disable iff (reset_i)
318                         $rose(clear_i) |-> (program_done_o ||
319                                             ((endc_state_r == ENDC_IDLE) && be_drained && !back_reg_valid_r)))
320                         else $error("back_end: clear_i while the back end still holds work");
321                     
322                       // consume requires wr_valid_r, ship_u2d requires wr_free -- they can
323                       // never coincide, so delta_acc_r never changes out from under the
324                       // snapshot delta takes of it.
325                       commit_ship_mutex: assert property (@(posedge clk_i) disable iff (reset_i)
326                         !(consume && ship_u2d))
327                         else $error("back_end: commit landed the same cycle ship_u2d fired");
328                     
329                       // ---- Front-end sequencing the back end relies on ----
330                       be_push_into_free_back_reg: assert property (@(posedge clk_i) disable iff (reset_i || clear_i)
331                         back_reg_push_i |-> back_reg_free_o)
332                         else $error("back_end: back_reg push while back_reg still holds a word");
333                     
334                       // RB + skid are only safe because the front end never forwards more than
335                       // one word ahead of the seam. A forward that isn't taken is lost; one that
336                       // lands in RB past a waiting skid entry reorders words.
337                       be_fwd_never_dropped: assert property (@(posedge clk_i) disable iff (reset_i || clear_i)
338                         read_fwd_valid_i |-> read_fwd_ready_o)
339                         else $error("back_end: read forward dropped (RB and skid both full)");
340                     
341                       be_fwd_keeps_order: assert property (@(posedge clk_i) disable iff (reset_i || clear_i)
342                         !(read_fwd_valid_i && rb_empty && skid_valid_r))
343                         else $error("back_end: read forward overtook the skid entry (word order lost)");
344                     
345                       be_endc_after_seam_drained: assert property (@(posedge clk_i) disable iff (reset_i || clear_i)
346                         endc_i |-> !back_reg_valid_r)
347                         else $error("back_end: ENDC while back_reg still holds a word");
348                     
349                       // ---- Datapath handoff (F9): the producer holds A/R31 until dp_ack_o ----
350                       be_dp_holds_until_ack: assert property (@(posedge clk_i) disable iff (reset_i || clear_i)
351                         (dp_valid_i && !dp_ack_o) |=> (dp_valid_i && $stable(accumulator_i) && $stable(guards_i)))
352                         else $error("back_end: dp_valid_i/accumulator_i/guards_i changed before dp_ack_o");
353                     
354                       // ---- VS response contract: a read's rsp arrives >= 1 cycle after its ack ----
355                       be_rsp_only_when_waiting: assert property (@(posedge clk_i) disable iff (reset_i || clear_i)
356                         vs_bus.rsp_valid |-> (rb_state_r == RB_WAIT_RESP))
357                         else $error("back_end: VS rsp_valid while RB is not waiting for one (response lost)");
358                     
359                       be_done_sticky: assert property (@(posedge clk_i) disable iff (reset_i)
360                         (program_done_o && !clear_i) |=> program_done_o)
361                         else $error("back_end: program_done_o dropped before clear_i");
362                     
363                       // ---- Each value-store bit is committed at most once per image ----
364                       // A second commit of a bit can take its old value from a read issued
365                       // before the first commit's write lands, so it compares against stale data
366                       // and silently drops its own update. The ISA makes that program malformed;
367                       // this shadow of every bit committed since reset/clear catches it.
368                       logic [WORD_WIDTH-1:0] committed_bits [logic [WIDX-1:0]];
369                       always @(posedge clk_i) begin
370        1/1              if (reset_i || clear_i) begin
371        1/1                committed_bits.delete();
372        1/1              end else if (consume) begin
373        1/1                if (committed_bits.exists(wr_addr_r)) begin
374                             be_bit_committed_once: assert ((committed_bits[wr_addr_r] & back_reg_r.field) == '0)
375                               else $error("back_end: word %h commits bits %h a second time this image (malformed)",
376                                           {wr_addr_r, 2'b00}, committed_bits[wr_addr_r] & back_reg_r.field);
377        0/1     ==>          committed_bits[wr_addr_r] = committed_bits[wr_addr_r] | back_reg_r.field;
378                           end else begin
379        1/1                  committed_bits[wr_addr_r] = back_reg_r.field;
380                           end
381                         end
                        MISSING_ELSE

347                         else $error("back_end: ENDC while back_reg still holds a word");
348                     
349                       // ---- Datapath handoff (F9): the producer holds A/R31 until dp_ack_o ----
350                       be_dp_holds_until_ack: assert property (@(posedge clk_i) disable iff (reset_i || clear_i)
351                         (dp_valid_i && !dp_ack_o) |=> (dp_valid_i && $stable(accumulator_i) && $stable(guards_i)))
352                         else $error("back_end: dp_valid_i/accumulator_i/guards_i changed before dp_ack_o");
353                     
354                       // ---- VS response contract: a read's rsp arrives >= 1 cycle after its ack ----
355                       be_rsp_only_when_waiting: assert property (@(posedge clk_i) disable iff (reset_i || clear_i)
356                         vs_bus.rsp_valid |-> (rb_state_r == RB_WAIT_RESP))
357                         else $error("back_end: VS rsp_valid while RB is not waiting for one (response lost)");
358                     
359                       be_done_sticky: assert property (@(posedge clk_i) disable iff (reset_i)
360                         (program_done_o && !clear_i) |=> program_done_o)
361                         else $error("back_end: program_done_o dropped before clear_i");
362                     
363                       // ---- Each value-store bit is committed at most once per image ----
364                       // A second commit of a bit can take its old value from a read issued
365                       // before the first commit's write lands, so it compares against stale data
366                       // and silently drops its own update. The ISA makes that program malformed;
367                       // this shadow of every bit committed since reset/clear catches it.
368                       logic [WORD_WIDTH-1:0] committed_bits [logic [WIDX-1:0]];
369                       always @(posedge clk_i) begin
370        1/1              if (reset_i || clear_i) begin
371        1/1                committed_bits.delete();
372        1/1              end else if (consume) begin
373        1/1                if (committed_bits.exists(wr_addr_r)) begin
374                             be_bit_committed_once: assert ((committed_bits[wr_addr_r] & back_reg_r.field) == '0)
375                               else $error("back_end: word %h commits bits %h a second time this image (malformed)",
376                                           {wr_addr_r, 2'b00}, committed_bits[wr_addr_r] & back_reg_r.field);
377        0/1     ==>          committed_bits[wr_addr_r] = committed_bits[wr_addr_r] | back_reg_r.field;
378                           end else begin
379        1/1                  committed_bits[wr_addr_r] = back_reg_r.field;
380                           end
381                         end
                        MISSING_ELSE
